title: Stable three-dimensional solitons in spin-orbit-coupled atomic-molecular condensates
authors: Chao Kong, Jinqing Li, Guihua Chen, Guilong Li, Zhaopin Chen, Haiming Deng, Boris A. Malomed, Yongyao Li
abstract: We elaborate a mechanism for the creation of stable three-dimensional (3D) solitons in spin-orbit-coupled (SOC) atomic-molecular Bose-Einstein condensate, modeled by the mean-field equations with the quadratic three-wave interaction, characterized by mismatch $α$. The planar (effectively two-dimensional) SOC is applied to the soliton's atomic component, structuring it as a mixed mode (MM) or semi-vortex (SV). The molecular component of the SV soliton is shaped as a 3D vortex, while the molecular component in the MM soliton is an MM too. The solitons exist up to a critical value of $α$. The system demonstrates a relatively large norm share of the vortex components, exceeding $50\%$ of the total norm, which is an essential feature of SOC-supported solitons. This is scheme for realizing stable vortex solitons in free space with the quadratic nonlinearity.
summary: This paper theoretically investigates stable three-dimensional soliton formation in spin-orbit-coupled atomic-molecular Bose-Einstein condensates. By modeling the system with coupled mean-field equations and analyzing specific mixed-mode and semi-vortex configurations, the authors demonstrate that SOC coupling stabilizes these structures. This work is significant because it provides a robust mechanism for realizing stable vortex solitons using quadratic nonlinearity in quantum gas systems.
main_problem: The research aims to elucidate a mechanism for creating stable three-dimensional (3D) solitons within spin-orbit-coupled (SOC) atomic-molecular Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs).
main_result: Stable 3D solitons, specifically Semi-Vortex (SV) and Mixed-Mode (MM) types, are demonstrated to exist in this SOC scheme, providing a method for realizing stable vortex solitons with quadratic nonlinearity.
method: The analysis uses the imaginary-time integration method on coupled Gross-Pitaevskii equations (GPEs), employing approximations like the cascading-limit approximation for strong detuning.
model_or_system: The system models an atomic-molecular BEC governed by mean-field equations incorporating quadratic three-wave interactions and SOC applied to the atomic components. The dynamics are described by coupled GPEs for the atomic ($\varphi_1, \varphi_2$) and molecular ($\psi$) fields.
key_observables: Topological charge (unit circulation in $\varphi_2$), vortex norm share ($F_v > 50\%$ of total norm), chemical potential ($\mu$), Energy ($E$), and Angular Momentum ($M_z$).
important_parameters: The control parameters are the particle number ($N$) and the mismatch parameter ($\alpha$); stability is mapped in the $(N, \alpha)$ plane.
main_assumptions: Key assumptions include applying planar (effectively 2D) SOC to the atomic component and utilizing the cascading-limit approximation for strong detuning.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate stable soliton structures (SV and MM) via density isosurfaces, map out stability regions in the $(N, \alpha)$ plane, and plot conserved quantities like $\mu, E,$ and $M_z$ versus particle number or detuning.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the governing coupled GPEs for the SOC-BEC. It then analyzes specific soliton ansätze (SV and MM) using numerical methods, mapping out their existence regions in parameter space and confirming stability through analysis of conserved quantities and vortex component dominance.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it extends the study of nonlinear wave phenomena into the realm of ultracold atomic gases. The stabilization mechanism provided by SOC coupling for 3D solitons, especially achieving a large vortex norm share, offers new theoretical pathways for controlling complex quantum matter waves.
